comparisons.peer_topic: Competitive landscape and determinants of product competitiveness
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD operates in a highly competitive market where timely delivery of latest products is critical for revenue growth. Key factors determining product competitiveness include total cost of ownership, performance, features (including AI accelerations), energy efficiency, and software compatibility.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and AMD both identify energy efficiency as a critical determinant of product competitiveness, though they frame it differently. Intel focuses on building energy efficiency into products to help customers lower emissions and costs as part of its environmental strategy (P066_S003). AMD explicitly lists energy efficiency (including power consumption and battery life) as one of the main factors determining product competitiveness, directly linking it to total cost of ownership (P063_S002). Both companies recognize that energy-efficient products provide customer value through reduced operational costs, aligning their commercial and environmental strategies, but AMD frames it primarily within a competitive market context while Intel frames it within a broader environmental responsibility and value chain impact context.

sentences.text: We build energy efficiency into our products to help our customers lower their own emissions, energy usage, and costs, and we collaborate with policymakers and other stakeholders to use technology to address environmental challenges.

We believe that the main factors that determine our product competitiveness are total cost of ownership, timely product introductions, product quality, product features and capabilities (including accelerations for key workloads such as AI), energy efficiency (including power consumption and battery life, given their impact on total cost of ownership), reliability, performance, size (or form factor), selling price, cost, adherence to industry standards (and the creation of open industry standards), level of integration, software and hardware compatibility, ease of use and functionality of software design tools, completeness of applicable software solutions, security and stability, brand recognition and availability.

comparisons.peer_summary: Micron proactively manages environmental compliance and sustainability, conforming its wafer fabrication facilities to the ISO 14001:2015 standard to ensure continuous performance improvement.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and Micron both address their approach to environmental compliance and sustainability, specifically noting engagement with stakeholders and adherence to rigorous standards. Intel collaborates with policymakers and stakeholders to address environmental challenges and focuses on addressing climate impacts in its value chain (P066_S003, P067_S003). Micron explicitly states that its approach to environmental compliance considers the expectations of customers, investors, and other stakeholders, and conforms to the ISO 14001:2015 standard (P083_S002, P083_S003, P083_S006). Both companies demonstrate a proactive stance toward environmental management involving stakeholder alignment and formal compliance frameworks, though Micron specifically cites ISO 14001 certification while Intel details its value chain focus.

sentences.text: We build energy efficiency into our products to help our customers lower their own emissions, energy usage, and costs, and we collaborate with policymakers and other stakeholders to use technology to address environmental challenges.
We also focus on addressing climate change impacts upstream and downstream in the value chain.

We approach environmental compliance and sustainability proactively to ensure we meet applicable government regulations regarding use of raw materials and chemicals, discharges, emissions, climate change and energy use, and waste disposal and management from our manufacturing processes.
Our approach also considers the expectations of our investors, customers, team members, community members, and other stakeholders.

As part of the ISO 14001 framework, we have established a global environmental policy and meet requirements, such as environmental aspects evaluation and control, compliance obligations, commitment, training, communication, document control, operational control, emergency preparedness and response, and management review.

comparisons.peer_topic: Product energy efficiency and Green500 performance
comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA's GPU-accelerated computing is optimized for energy efficiency and performance per watt. The company powered 24 of the top 30 most energy-efficient systems on the Green500 list, including the top supercomputer.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and NVIDIA disclose specific strategies and performance metrics regarding product energy efficiency as a core component of their environmental and competitive strategy. Intel emphasizes building energy efficiency into products to help customers lower emissions and leveraging its technology to enable other sectors to reduce climate footprints (P066_S003, P067_S004). Similarly, NVIDIA highlights that its GPU-accelerated computing is optimized for energy efficiency and performance per watt, evidencing this through its strong presence on the Green500 list of the most energy-efficient systems (P061_S002, P061_S003, P061_S004). Both companies use product-level energy efficiency as a key value proposition and environmental action, though NVIDIA specifically cites external ranking performance (Green500) while Intel focuses on the broader enablement and customer benefit.

sentences.text: We build energy efficiency into our products to help our customers lower their own emissions, energy usage, and costs, and we collaborate with policymakers and other stakeholders to use technology to address environmental challenges.

This includes improving product energy efficiency and increasing the positive impact of our products by leveraging opportunities for Intel technologies to enable other sectors of the economy to reduce their climate and energy footprints.
GPU-accelerated computing is inherently more energy efficient than traditional computing for many workloads because it is optimized for throughput, performance per watt, and certain AI workloads.
The energy efficiency of our products is evidenced by our continued strong presence on the Green500 list of the most energy-efficient systems.
We powered 24 of the top 30 most energy efficient systems, including the top supercomputer, on the Green500 list.

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm has established science-based emissions reduction targets approved by the SBTi, including a 50% reduction in absolute Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 2030, a 25% reduction in absolute Scope 3 GHG emissions by 2030, and reaching net-zero GHG emissions across the value chain by 2040.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and Qualcomm both disclose formal, science-based targets for reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions across their operations and value chains. Intel states it takes action on emissions reduction strategies focused on abatement and addresses climate change impacts upstream and downstream in the value chain (P067_S001, P067_S003). Qualcomm provides specific quantitative targets approved by the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), including a 50% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions and a 25% reduction in Scope 3 (value chain) emissions by 2030, with a net-zero goal by 2040 (P062_S001, P062_S002). While Intel describes the strategic areas of focus, Qualcomm provides the specific numerical milestones, but both affirm a commitment to science-based emissions reduction strategies covering their operational and value chain footprints.

sentences.text: We continue to take action on emissions reduction strategies focused on emissions abatement, and to make additional investments in renewable electricity, process and equipment optimization, and energy conservation.
We also focus on addressing climate change impacts upstream and downstream in the value chain.

Qualcomm has established near- and long-term science-based emissions reduction targets, which have been approved by the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), including: (1) reduce absolute Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 50% by 2030 from a 2020 base year; (2) reduce absolute Scope 3 GHG emissions by 25% by 2030 from a 2020 base year; and (3) reach net-zero GHG emissions across the value chain by 2040.
